claims.text: Sample Consistency methods outperformed Token Level Probability and Confidence Elicitation methods for estimating LLM uncertainty in medical tasks.
Sample Consistency by Sentence Embedding achieved discrimination performance of ROC AUC 0.68–0.79.
Sample Consistency by Sentence Embedding exhibited poor calibration.
Sample Consistency by GPT Annotation achieved discrimination performance of ROC AUC 0.66–0.74.
Sample Consistency by GPT Annotation achieved more accurate calibration than Sample Consistency by Sentence Embedding.
Nearly all evaluated uncertainty metrics had better discriminative performance with diagnosis questions than with treatment selection questions.
Verbalized confidence through Confidence Elicitation consistently over-estimates LLM confidence.

evidence.description: Sample Consistency methods outperformed Token Level Probability and Confidence Elicitation methods across evaluated patient scenario datasets.
Sample Consistency by Sentence Embedding achieved the highest discrimination performance with ROC AUC 0.68–0.79.
Sample Consistency by Sentence Embedding achieved high discrimination with poor raw calibration.
Sample Consistency by GPT Annotation achieved second-best discrimination with ROC AUC 0.66–0.74.
Sample Consistency by GPT Annotation achieved second-best discrimination with more accurate calibration.
Nearly all uncertainty metrics had better discriminative performance with diagnosis rather than treatment selection questions.
Verbalized confidence (Confidence Elicitation) was found to consistently over-estimate model confidence.

methodologies.name: LLM Uncertainty Metric Comparative Evaluation
methodologies.description: Evaluated Confidence Elicitation, Token Level Probability, and Sample Consistency metrics on discrimination and calibration properties across multiple LLMs for medical diagnosis and treatment selection.
datasets: Three datasets of open-ended patient scenarios

limitations.text: Sample Consistency by Sentence Embedding suffers from poor calibration, requiring reference cases to re-calibrate results.
Uncertainty metrics demonstrate lower discriminative performance when applied to treatment selection questions compared to diagnosis questions.
Confidence Elicitation consistently over-estimates LLM confidence when verbalizing uncertainty.
